title: Incremental rules validator and compiler for region/tier/fallback policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The current routing-rule validation logic lives in several places (runtime loader, admin linting, and the console preview). This has caused inconsistent error messages, missed edge-cases during canary rollouts, and intermittent production fallthroughs when a regional selector and fallback set interact. Goal: Build an incremental validator+compiler that can run in three modes: 1) strict linting for CI/console with actionable diagnostics, 2) lightweight runtime verifier for fast startup checks, and 3) a canonical compiler that emits a deterministic, versioned intermediate representation (IR) used by the router for low-latency decisioning. The work here focuses on the schema/DSL validation, staged compiler, and migration hooks required for a gradual switchover. Out of scope: policy UI changes and autoscaler tuning.
acceptance_criteria:
- A validator library (Go) that performs schema + semantic checks and returns structured diagnostics with line/char locations for DSL files.
- Compiler produces a compact IR (JSON) with stable keys for region selectors, tier ranges, and fallback model variant chains.
- Validator integrated into CI so any rejected policy prevents deploys to staging/constrained environments.
- Runtime verifier accepts the IR and runs a fast safety check within 10ms per policy on average.
- Migration harness that can import existing policies and emit a compatibility report with automatic fixes for common patterns.
- Unit and integration tests covering parsing, ambiguous selector resolution, and fallback determinism.
- Documentation and console preview updated to reference the new validator and the IR versioning scheme.
implementation_plan:
1) Build parser and schema validator using an existing PEG grammar (forked from policy-transpiler).
2) Add semantic passes: name resolution, region/tier reference checks, and variant compatibility checks.
3) Implement a deterministic compiler that lowers validated AST to IR v1.0.
4) Create a runtime verifier library that loads IR v1.0 and performs micro-checks used at process start and during hot-reload.
5) Add CI lint step and a console preview hook that calls the strict linting API.
6) Provide a migration tool (CLI) to convert legacy policies and emit a compatibility report and optional autofixes.
7) Run canary with selected customers and monitor deterministic fallback metrics.
Tasks: parser (Diego), semantic checks (Lina Chen), compiler (Santiago Ruiz), runtime verifier (Diego), CI integration (Kate Nguyen), docs (Samir Desai).
migration_plan:
- Phase 0: Add validator to CI in warning mode. Collect failure rates and common patterns.
- Phase 1: Enable strict mode for new policy uploads and console edits (errors block save).
- Phase 2: Run an automated conversion job for existing policies with safe autofixes and surface manual review items in a console migration dashboard.
- Phase 3: Switch router ingestion to IR v1.0 behind a feature flag. Gradually enable for non-critical regions.
- Phase 4: Guarded global rollout once telemetry shows <0.1% change in routing decisions and no customer errors.
Rollback: keep legacy parser active and accept both formats for 4 weeks after rollout.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for parser edge-cases: nested selectors, deprecated fields, and conflicting tier definitions.
- Semantic tests: ambiguous fallback chains, region aliases, and precedence rules.
- Fuzzing harness for schema inputs generated from production corpora.
- Integration tests: CI lint step against a corpus of 2k real policies, verify IR parity with legacy outputs for 95% of cases.
- Performance: runtime verifier latency targets (p95 < 12ms).
- E2E canary: route 1% of traffic through router using IR v1.0 and compare routing decisions and tail-latency to baseline for 48h.
rollout_plan:
- Internal alpha: core infra and small set of test policies (1 week).
- Staged canary: enable IR v1.0 ingestion in eu-west and us-east for non-critical customers (2 weeks).
- Expand canary: add us-west and ap-southeast with production-sized traffic (2 weeks).
- Full roll: flip feature flag globally after monitoring window and stakeholder signoff.
- Post-roll: deprecation of legacy parser after 28 days.
risk_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Compiler introduces subtle precedence changes that alter production routing. Mitigation: exhaustive diff tests between legacy and new IR on sample of historical policy snapshots; keep both parsers active until validated.
- Risk: Validator blocks large number of existing policies. Mitigation: staged warning-first rollout and autofix rules to address common cases.
- Risk: Performance regression during hot-reload. Mitigation: micro-benchmarks for verifier and provide fallback path to legacy runtime on startup failure.
- Risk: Security issues around policy injection. Mitigation: sanitize all diagnostics, require auth for migration jobs, and run security review for any CLI that writes policies (not required for this ticket but flagged for follow-up).
